settings.fallback_alt: Shalini standing beside a large abstract canvas in her studio
settings.heading: A practice rooted in attention.
settings.text:
Shalini is a contemporary painter working from an intuitive language of colour, gesture, and natural form. Her paintings ask what remains when a landscape becomes memory.

Each canvas is built through accumulation and erasure—earth pigments, charcoal, oils, and thin washes finding their way into a quiet, tactile whole.

settings.label: In the artist’s words
settings.quote: I paint the feeling before the words arrive.

settings.fallback_alt: Close-up of layered paint and botanical marks
settings.heading: Nothing begins with a finished picture.
settings.text: There are only first marks, a remembered colour, and the willingness to follow. The work arrives slowly, through looking and listening.

settings.fallback_alt: Pigment bowls and brushes on the studio worktable
settings.heading: Between intuition and observation.
settings.text: Shalini’s practice moves between intuition and observation. Every work begins with colour, then finds its own rhythm through mark, texture, erasure, and time.

settings.fallback_alt: Detail from the Earth Song collection
settings.heading: Colour as a kind of remembering.
settings.text: Built slowly in layers of mineral pigment, charcoal, and translucent washes, these works hold the trace of weather, wild gardens, and remembered places.
